If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) and price is trending upward, increase forecast by 1.0–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.34–0.66) and true price diverges sharply from forecast, apply a 2.0–3.0% downward correction in late horizon (16–30 days) to align with reversal signals.  
When sentiment spikes to 1.00 and price is below 65.00, add a 1.5–2.0% upward bias to forecast for early horizon to reflect bullish sentiment.  
If sentiment is consistently 0.00 across 5+ days, apply a 2.5–3.5% downward bias to forecast for mid horizon to reflect lack of conviction.  
If true price exceeds forecast by >5% in late horizon and sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for next period to avoid overcorrection.
